podcast.title: Collaboration with Daniel Lanois
podcast.body: Daniel Lanois applied his learned recording techniques from Brian Eno to sessions with bands like The Parachute Club. "Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."

podcast.title: Emergence as Serious Stars
podcast.body: Parachute Club emerged as one of the serious stars through the late 1970s and into the 1980s, benefiting from the new industry infrastructure and increased radio support for Canadian talent. This period marked a shift towards greater national and international success for homegrown artists. "Love her boy, Chilla Wack, Bruce Coburn, rough trade, the pay-all was Toronto, the headpins, the spoons, bride-adams, parachute club, men without hats, Cory Hart. They all emerged as serious stars through the late 1970s and into the 1980s."

podcast.title: Grant Avenue Studios Recording Artists
podcast.body: The Parachute Club recorded material at Grant Avenue Studios around 1983-84, when David Botrell was starting as an assistant. "Martha and the Muffins in the parachute club and Luba. Those records were going on while I was there."

xref.title: Client Base Growth
xref.body: After relocating to the Hamilton house, the studio's client base expanded significantly, attracting numerous Canadian artists like Martha and the Muffins, The Parachute Club, and Bruce Cockburn. "That's where their client base increased exponentially."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Legendary Recording Studios

xref.title: Collaboration with Daniel Lanois
xref.body: Impressed by Daniel Lanois's production of a "Time Twins" track, Brian Eno booked studio time with Lanois at Grand Avenue to work on his early ambient records, thereby mentoring Lanois in recording music. "Eno was so impressed that he booked time with Dan at Grand Avenue to work on some of his early ambient records and over the next couple of years Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mentorship by Brian Eno
xref.body: Brian Eno, impressed by a track Lanois produced for Time Twins, booked studio time with Lanois at Grand Avenue. Over several years, Lanois gained extensive knowledge about recording music while working on Eno's early ambient records. "Eno was so impressed that he booked time with Dan at Grand Avenue to work on some of his early ambient records and over the next couple of years Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."
